structuralProjection.cellText: trimmed visible cells with fixture paths, model ids, model prose, and the deterministic workspace/branch projection applied
structuralProjection.ansi: raw ANSI retained as captured evidence only; verification compares resolved cell presentation, never raw ANSI byte parity
structuralProjection.sgr: ordered SGR tokens are retained as diagnostic evidence; resolved cell style is the comparison authority, compared as the semantic theme role each color resolves to on its own runtime palette (issue #797), while a color no single semantic role resolves stays at its exact truecolor value
structuralProjection.screenshot: themeParity.renderedScreenshots retains the rendered terminal cell rows as text screenshots
structuralProjection.scrollback: scrollback cell rows are compared separately from the visible viewport; the profileProjection comparison is length-compensated, discounting a height surplus only up to the profile rows one runtime removed from its viewport, and records the per-barrier discount as scrollbackLengthCompensation
structuralProjection.profile: resolved projection removes exact pi runtime-identity/startup-documentation rows and isolates provider usage for user-message, status-footer, tool-result, and scrollback
structuralProjection.omission: declared pi-only rows are removed only with explicit patterns; the resolved styled-cell projection decides whether the remaining delta is intentional
structuralProjection.verification: --verify checks reproducible report digests and one explicit triage classification per scenario; product defects remain visible in child issues

profileProjection.role: diagnostic evidence; resolved comparison also uses styled cells after this profile

omissions: pi's action-handler map on the editor component has no C++ EditorComponent counterpart; recorded as a capability difference with its count
pi re-assigns borderColor twice per border-token change at install; Pike applies one TextStyleHook per token change, so the first-install assignment counts differ by design

triage.rationale: Both runtimes install a probe extension editor through the real extension-UI registration the product builds for a session's prompt slot, and reproduce the frozen audit-1051 contract: factory inputs present (tui/theme/keybindings), factory called once per install (2 total), submit/change callbacks copied before the first text transfer, text and focus transferred at install, padding/autocomplete options applied exactly once per install, the border token follows thinking-level and Bash-mode changes, restore carries the prompt to the default editor with no second editor rendered, reinstall transfers the prompt slot's text and focus, and submit clears the editor through the copied submit sink. The compared authority is that lifecycle contract (resolved border RGB, transfer and option facts), because the two probe editors draw different chrome: pi's CustomEditor renders its own frame while the Pike probe renders an ext-editor row, so the settled cells stay evidence. Expectations come from the frozen pi-v1.3.0 run only; Pike never regenerates them.
acceptedDifferences: pi's editor component carries an app-action-handler map (16 entries in the frozen capture); the C++ EditorComponent contract has no action-handler facet, so the count is recorded as a capability difference (issue #1033).

pi's install path assigns borderColor twice per border-token change (6 assignments in the first install's lifetime); Pike applies one TextStyleHook per token change (4 in the first install's lifetime). The token follow itself compares exactly, including the resolved RGB of each border sample.

Pike restore/reinstall run through the reload-family re-apply path (the refreshed registration context installs none, then installs again), the reachable Pike counterpart of pi's setEditorComponent(undefined/factory) shortcut; the carried-text, single-editor and focus facts are compared exactly.
